name: Joseph A. Ferris
bio: Joseph A. Ferris was a Medora merchant who in February 1884 reported his cattle wintering without loss and in March went to Mandan to buy dry goods for a new store. Through 1884 he added groceries, a new store room across the river and a warehouse for his stock. In June 1885 he began a two-story store building on Main Street, opened it with a house-warming dance in early August, and moved his goods in that month; the paper also reported a building put up for Mrs. Malloy on one of his lots. He married in New Brunswick in January 1886, was named for probate judge on the Stockmen's Ticket that March but withdrew, became Medora's sole agent for Collins' goods in April, and in June sued Mrs. P. Malloy for possession of property.
